publisher: TheMoroccoAI.com (independent; not affiliated with the Government of Morocco)

classifications.VERIFIED FACT: An event, act or status that the cited source documents directly (for example, a signature, a launch or an appointment).
classifications.OFFICIAL TARGET: A quantified goal set by an official body. It is not an outcome and must not be read as achieved.
classifications.ANNOUNCED PLAN: A programme, institution or product an official body has announced or presented, whose operational delivery the registry has not verified.
classifications.INDEPENDENT ANALYSIS: An inference drawn by TheMoroccoAI from two or more records. It is labelled as interpretation, not as fact.
classifications.UNVERIFIED CLAIM: A statement attributed to a source whose underlying data the registry has not independently checked.

verification_statuses.verified: The source page was retrieved on the retrieval date and the excerpt was matched against it.
verification_statuses.partial: The source was retrieved but does not by itself carry every detail of the claim; the limitation is stated in verification_note.

records.title: Official launch of the national strategy "Maroc Digital 2030"
records.source_organization: MAP (Maghreb Arabe Presse), MAP Express
records.claim: The national strategy Digital Morocco 2030 (Maroc Digital 2030) was officially launched in Rabat on 25 September 2024 by the Ministry of Digital Transition and Administration Reform.

Cette stratégie, lancée par le ministère de la Transition numérique et de la Réforme de l'administration

records.title: Digital Morocco 2030: stated job and e-government objectives
records.source_organization: MAP (Maghreb Arabe Presse), MAP Express
records.claim: Digital Morocco 2030 sets the objectives of 240,000 direct jobs with a contribution to GDP in 2030, digitalising public services, and moving Morocco from 113th to 50th place worldwide in the e-government development index.

digitaliser les services publics. Le but étant de faire passer le Maroc de la 113e à la 50e place mondiale dans l'indice de développement du e-gouvernement
records.verification_note: The source does not give a separate target year for the e-government ranking objective; 2030 is the strategy horizon.

records.title: Head of Government statement on public digital investment, 2021–2024

records.title: Synthesis report of the First National AI Conference: Al Jazari Institute memorandum (Nador)

a procédé à la signature de la convention constitutive du Groupement d’Intérêt Public (GIP) “Institut Jazari ROOT”, aux côtés de plusieurs départements ministériels et d’institutions publiques

le développement de solutions innovantes reposant sur l’intelligence artificielle, l’Internet des objets, la robotique avancée et l’analyse des données industrielles

records.title: JAZARI network announced across the twelve regions; JAZARI ROOT as its core

records.title: Morocco AI 2030 roadmap: 2030 targets
records.source_organization: Maroc.ma (national portal of the Kingdom of Morocco)
records.claim: The Morocco AI 2030 roadmap, presented by the Ministry of Digital Transition and Administration Reform, sets 2030 targets of MAD 100 billion in added value to GDP, 50,000 direct and indirect jobs, and 200,000 trained and certified AI talents.

records.title: Morocco AI 2030 roadmap: pillars and the JAZARI Institutes network

source_excerpts: Morocco’s Ministry of Digital Transition and Administration Reform on Tuesday in Rabat presented the main advances under the "Morocco AI 2030" roadmap

Its implementation notably relies on the national network of JAZARI Institutes, the operational arm for AI research and innovation, comprising JAZARI ROOT, JAZARI Smart City, JAZARI EduTech and JAZARI Industrie X.0.
records.verification_note: The fact recorded is how the ministry described the roadmap's structure. The registry has no separate signed instrument for JAZARI Smart City or JAZARI EduTech.

records.title: Atlas-Chat: Adapting Large Language Models for Low-Resource Moroccan Arabic Dialect (arXiv:2409.17912)
records.source_organization: arXiv (Shang et al.)
records.claim: A preprint first submitted on 26 September 2024 introduces Atlas-Chat, large language models for Moroccan Arabic (Darija) in 2B, 9B and 27B sizes, fine-tuned on an instruction dataset built by consolidating existing Darija resources, creating new manual and synthetic data, and translating English instructions.
source_excerpts: Atlas-Chat: Adapting Large Language Models for Low-Resource Moroccan Arabic Dialect

Focusing on Moroccan Arabic, also known as Darija, we construct our instruction dataset by consolidating existing Darija language resources, creating novel datasets both manually and synthetically, and translating English instructions with stringent quality control.
Atlas-Chat-2B, 9B, and 27B models, fine-tuned on the dataset
records.verification_note: A preprint, not peer-reviewed in this record. The abstract's priority claim ("first-ever") and benchmark comparisons are the authors' own and are not recorded as facts.

records.title: DarijaBERT model card
records.source_organization: Hugging Face (SI2M-Lab organisation)
records.claim: DarijaBERT is published on Hugging Face as a joint release of AIOX Lab and the SI2M Lab of INSEA: a model for written Moroccan Darija based on the BERT-base architecture without next-sentence-prediction pre-training, trained on about 3 million Darija sequences (691MB of text, about 100M tokens).
source_excerpts: AIOX Lab and SI2M Lab INSEA have joined forces
It is based on the same architecture as BERT-base, but without the Next Sentence Prediction (NSP) objective.
This model was trained on a total of ~3 Million sequences of Darija dialect representing 691MB of text or a total of ~100M tokens.
records.verification_note: Publication date left blank: the Hugging Face API reports 2022-03-02, the placeholder it assigns to repositories created before that date. The card's priority claim ("first BERT model") is not recorded. The card cites a 2023 paper by Gaanoun et al. that was not retrieved.

records.title: Al-Atlas-0.5B model card

Its 2023 statement about an FDA submission is consistent with, but does not by itself identify, the applicant of FDA 510(k) K242594 (MAI-EV-0032).

records.title: DeepEcho website: product description and regulatory disclaimer
records.source_organization: DeepEcho
records.claim: DeepEcho describes its software as using AI and deep learning to help radiologists and minimally trained clinicians with ultrasound video diagnosis, and states on its website that its claims and metrics are not yet validated by the FDA and come from its own clinical studies under scientific and regulatory review.
source_excerpts: Deepecho uses Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning to mimic what a trained sonographer would do and help radiologists and minimally trained clinicians with ultrasound video diagnosis.
Claims, figures, metrics & any kind of scientific and / or marketing materials listed in the current website are not validated yet by the FDA.
Metrics comes from our own clinical studies (currently under scientific & regulatory review)
records.verification_note: The disclaimer is quoted as the site showed it on the retrieval date, but it appears outdated: the FDA database lists 510(k) clearance K242594 for a DEEPECHO device on 23 May 2025 (MAI-EV-0032, MAI-EV-0039), and the Moroccan government says DeepEcho's solution obtained FDA "approbation" (MAI-EV-0033). It is therefore no longer used to establish a lifecycle stage: a quotation that still matches its source can support a claim that is no longer current. Accuracy and speed figures on the site are self-reported and not recorded.

records.title: FDA 510(k) K242594: clearance letter and 510(k) summary for DEEPECHO
records.source_organization: U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)
records.claim: The FDA's letter of 23 May 2025, addressed to DeepEcho at a Dover, Delaware address, determines that the DEEPECHO device is substantially equivalent to legally marketed predicate devices for the stated indications for use, so that the company may market it subject to general controls. The 510(k) summary describes DEEPECHO as cloud-based software that uses machine learning to detect standard fetal biometry views and assist in computing fetal biometric measurements, for trained healthcare professionals; gives a contact e-mail address on the deepecho.io domain; and states that training data came in part from sites in Morocco and test data in part from Casablanca.

deepecho.io
Training data were obtained from two Roshan MFM clinics in New York City and selected sites in Morocco.

records.verification_note: Primary regulatory document. A 510(k) clearance permits marketing in the United States; the FDA distinguishes it from premarket approval (PMA). It is not a finding of clinical outcomes and does not authorise or show use in Morocco. The shared web domain and Moroccan data sites associate the applicant with the deepecho.io developer that UM6P Ventures describes as Morocco-based (MAI-EV-0028), but no source establishes their legal relationship.

records.title: TOUBKAL: peer-reviewed description of the system and its reported workloads
records.source_organization: The Journal of Supercomputing (Springer)
records.claim: A peer-reviewed article in The Journal of Supercomputing, by authors affiliated with Mohammed VI Polytechnic University's College of Computing, describes Toubkal's GPU partitions (NVIDIA A100 nodes from the initial 2022 deployment and H100 nodes added in 2025). It states that fine-tuning of transformer-based large language models and large-scale computational fluid dynamics simulations have been run on the system, and presents as a benchmark the fine-tuning runs, attributed to Belkasmi et al., that produced the GemMaroc Moroccan Darija language models.
source_excerpts: TOUBKAL: a high-performance supercomputer powering scientific research in Africa
The initial deployment in 2022 included five Dell XE8545 nodes with dual AMD EPYC 7713 CPUs and four NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB GPUs per node.
In 2025, three Dell XE8640 nodes were added, each with dual Intel Xeon Platinum 8468 CPUs and four NVIDIA H100-HBM3-80GB GPUs.

we examine practical workloads such as fine-tuning transformer-based large language models (LLMs) and conducting large-scale computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, both of which have been successfully run on Toubkal.
we present a practical benchmark demonstrating the fine-tuning of a large language model (LLM) performed on the Toubkal supercomputer by Belkasmi et al.
This work led to the creation of GemMaroc
records.verification_note: Open-access article (CC BY 4.0), published online 3 October 2025. Every author lists an affiliation with the university that hosts and runs Toubkal, so the workload statement is the operator's own report, peer-reviewed but not independent. It documents specific fine-tuning runs (the GemMaroc study by Belkasmi et al., which the registry has not retrieved), not the scale, share or continuity of AI use. The article's user counts and utilisation figures are not recorded. Benchmark, accuracy and energy figures in the article are not recorded. The verified fact is what the article states. Excerpts were matched against the article page retrieved on the retrieval date; automated requests to the publisher can receive a bot-challenge page, which the source checker reports as blocked and does not bypass.
